newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy posts loss for quarter; sees better results ahead.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy posts loss for quarter; sees better results ahead.

text.p: Best Buy Co. Inc., the consumer electronics retailer, Wednesday reported a loss for the latest quarter but forecast better results in the months ahead.
The company said it lost $2.6 million, or 6 cents a share, in its 1998 fiscal first quarter vs. a profit of $409,000, or 1 cent per share, a year earlier.
Sales dropped 2 percent to $1.60 billion from $1.63 billion a year ago.
"Despite the difficult market, our overall financial performance was better than we expected for the quarter," said Richard Schulze, chief executive officer.
He said the company's profit margin for the quarter was 15.4 percent, an increase of 1.2 percent from a year earlier.

"We expect that as we move into the seasonally higher volume second half of the fiscal year and continue to build upon our initiatives to improve profits, our operating performance will strongly improve over fiscal 1997," he said.
Best Buy said it plans to open 13 stores this year. Two were opened in the first quarter, six more are scheduled this quarter and the rest will be launched in the third quarter, the company said.
Best Buy's stock was up 62.5 cents at $12.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
